issues.legal_issue: A notification issued under an omitted provision continues to apply when that provision is replaced by a substantially corresponding provision.
material_facts: An earlier provision authorized the declaration of areas as urban areas for an industrial-relocation tax relief scheme, and a notification had declared the relevant area to be urban for that scheme.
The earlier tax-relief provision was omitted and replaced by a new provision providing relief for shifting an industrial undertaking from an urban area to a non-urban area.
The replacement provision included an urban-area definition substantially corresponding to the earlier definition.
The taxpayer sought relief under the replacement scheme based on a transfer from the area covered by the earlier notification.
issues.conclusion: The earlier notification continued under the replacement provision, so the taxpayer could rely on it to establish that the transfer was from an urban area.
issues.legal_principle: Section 24 of the General Clauses Act, 1897 continues subordinate legislation made under an enactment that is repealed and re-enacted, unless it is inconsistent with the re-enacted provision. The Court held that omission and re-enactment with modification attracted Section 24, and that the notification remained operative under the replacement scheme. It also held that repeal can occur by express omission or by implication: State of Orissa v. M.A. Tulloch & Co. (1964) 4 SCR 461; Ratan Lal Adukia v. Union of India (1989) 3 SCC 537; Poonjabhai Vanmalidas v. Commissioner of Income Tax, Ahmedabad, 1992 Supp. (1) SCC 182; State of Punjab v. Harnek Singh (2002) 3 SCC 481; and CIT v. Venkateswara Hatcheries (P) Ltd. (1999) 3 SCC 632. The Court explained that the contrary observations in Rayala Corporation (P) Ltd. v. Director of Enforcement (1969) 2 SCC 412 and Kolhapur Canesugar Works Ltd. v. Union of India (2000) 2 SCC 536 about omission and repeal under Section 6 did not preclude this result, including in light of Section 6A of the General Clauses Act.

rule.if: tax_relief_claim_under_replacement_scheme and earlier_notification_issued_under_old_scheme and old_scheme_omitted_and_replaced and replacement_scheme_covers_same_subject

predicates.tax_relief_claim_under_replacement_schem: The proceeding concerns a claim for tax relief under a statutory scheme that replaced an earlier scheme.
predicates.earlier_notification_issued_under_old_sc: A competent authority issued a notification under the earlier scheme to identify an area for the scheme's purposes.
predicates.old_scheme_omitted_and_replaced: The earlier scheme was omitted and a replacement scheme was enacted.
predicates.replacement_scheme_covers_same_subject: The replacement scheme addresses substantially the same subject as the earlier scheme.

issues.definition: When a tax-relief claim concerns a replacement scheme covering the same subject as an omitted scheme under which an area notification was issued, the notification continues under the replacement scheme.

issues.legal_issue: Amounts advanced toward acquiring or purchasing replacement business assets count as use of capital gains for industrial-relocation relief even if the assets have not yet been acquired in the same assessment year.
material_facts: The taxpayer sold assets of an industrial undertaking while shifting the undertaking from an urban area to a non-urban area.
Within the relevant period, the taxpayer paid advances to different persons for land, plant and machinery, and construction of a factory building.
The advances were made toward the purposes for which the capital gains could be reinvested, and the amount advanced exceeded the capital gain claimed for relief.
The revenue denied relief because the assets had not been purchased or acquired in the assessment year and the gains had not been deposited in the prescribed account.
issues.conclusion: The advances amounted to use of the capital gains for the specified acquisition and purchase purposes, and the taxpayer was entitled to the claimed relief.
issues.legal_principle: Section 54G(1) of the Income Tax Act, 1961 allows a period extending up to three years after the transfer to purchase new machinery or plant, acquire land or a building, or construct a building for the shifted undertaking. Under Section 54G(2), gains not used for those purposes before filing the return must be deposited in the prescribed account; the provision does not require the qualifying purchase or acquisition to be completed in the same assessment year as the transfer. Advances paid toward purchasing or acquiring the specified assets constitute use of the gains for those purposes. The Court relied on the text and structure of Section 54G(1) and (2).

predicates.industrial_relocation_tax_relief_claim: The proceeding concerns a claim for tax relief connected with shifting an industrial undertaking from an urban area to a non-urban area.
predicates.gains_arose_from_transfer_of_business_as: The claimed gains arose from transferring assets used for the business of the industrial undertaking in connection with its relocation.
predicates.proceeds_advanced_toward_qualifying_repl: The taxpayer paid advances from the gains toward purchasing or acquiring replacement assets for the relocated undertaking.

issues.definition: For an industrial-relocation tax-relief claim, advances of gains toward qualifying replacement assets count as use of those gains for those assets.
